floors.cause: Accuracy is met (35 of 43); wrong answers miss by one (2 of 37 answered, 5.4%). Both wrong answers are questions the intent grammar cannot express (a ratio, two date fields in one series), where the model answered a nearby question instead of refusing. Of its 6 refusals, 5 are correct refusals of such questions; 1 (fs-038) is a misread after one intent failed validation.
floors.next: v0.2 changes the prompt and the grammar, then measures them on a fresh run. The v0.1 prompt is not changed after seeing these results.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs the difference between two dates (opened to completed). Refused correctly, naming the missing duration. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs the difference between two dates (opened to completed). Refused, by failing validation twice.
misses.refusal: The registry cannot compute elapsed days between opened_at and completed_at. Metrics aggregate a single field, and no duration field exists. Average labour hours for urgent work orders is available instead, if that helps.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs a ratio of two counts. The model returned work order counts per status instead of refusing: a wrong answer, not a refusal. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs a ratio of two counts. The model returned two counts of cancelled orders instead of refusing: a wrong answer, not a refusal.

Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs a computed value (quantity times unit price). Refused correctly. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs a computed value (quantity times unit price). Refused, by failing validation twice.
misses.refusal: Parts revenue requires multiplying quantity by unit_price per line, and the registry metrics only aggregate a single field. No product or computed revenue measure is available.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs two date fields in one monthly series. The model counted completions among the orders opened each month instead of refusing: a wrong answer. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs two date fields in one monthly series. Refused, by failing validation twice.
Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs a distinct count of months in HAVING. Refused correctly. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs a distinct count of months in HAVING. Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: The registry can't express a per-technician check that every month in the quarter has at least one completion. A grouped query can't require all months to be present, and count_distinct on completed_at counts distinct timestamps, not distinct months.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): The first intent named a field that does not exist; on the retry the model said invoices cannot be grouped by customer. They can: the registry links invoices to customers through work orders and sites. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): The model left out the "paid" filter and grouped by site and customer ID instead of by customer, with no "more than $20,000" condition.
misses.refusal: The registry has no direct link from invoices to customers. Invoices join only to work_orders, and customers are reachable only through work_orders and sites, a multi-step path that the registry cannot group by. Customer totals cannot be computed from the listed fields.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs date arithmetic and a ratio. Refused correctly. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs date arithmetic and a ratio. Refused, by failing validation twice.
misses.refusal: The registry has no way to express an elapsed-time comparison (completed_at within 2 days of opened_at) or a share computed from two counts. Filters can only compare a field to a fixed value or another field directly, not to a date plus an interval.

misses.note: Haiku 5.5 (select-haiku-2026-11-11): Needs an anti-join (sites with no work orders). Refused correctly. mistral-small (select-2026-11-11): Needs an anti-join (sites with no work orders). Refused correctly.
misses.refusal: The registry cannot express 'sites with no work orders in a period'. That needs an anti-join from sites to work_orders, and the only listed relationship runs from work_orders to sites, so it cannot be filtered by the absence of related work orders.
